question_text: Find the equation of the circle with (4,2), (1,5) as ends of a diameter.

insider_note: The diameter form (x − x₁)(x − x₂) + (y − y₁)(y − y₂) = 0 saves finding the centre and the radius at all — using the long route costs time on a 2-mark question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the diameter form
steps.margin_note: One mark. x with x, y with y — never mix a given x-coordinate into the y bracket.
steps.memory_tip: Diameter form: (x − x₁)(x − x₂) + (y − y₁)(y − y₂) = 0.
lines: The circle with A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) as ends
steps.why: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so for any point P on the circle the lines PA and PB are perpendicular. Writing that condition in coordinates gives exactly this product form.
common_mistakes: Finding the centre and radius first, which takes far longer.

steps.label: Substitute and expand
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two small expansions and one collection; the constant is 4 + 10 = 14.
steps.why: Each bracket expands to a quadratic whose middle coefficient is minus the sum of the two values and whose constant is their product. A check: the centre (5/2, 7/2) is the midpoint of AB, as it must be.
common_mistakes: Getting the middle term as +5x by adding instead of subtracting.
Multiplying the two brackets together instead of adding them.
